Rather, remove this sin from the midst as well, as though it were a mighty barrier built up against them, and see that the gift is carried across unhindered to those in need. For sin itself is a disease more grievous than the other

pains, and it needs your help, or rather your visitation. You have authority against it too, since by your very deeds you became sharers with those who received this promise. Your acceptable [prayer] is strong — this is beyond all doubt — with the cooperation of those in need, to remove this disease as well as the others and to restore the sick to true health. Since, then, by God's providence you hold the victory over all afflictions, imitate the goodness of him who provided it, even toward those who are guilty. By persistent intercessions dissolve the liabilities incurred by sins. Release those fettered by long-standing diseases. Be moved to take pleasure in the choice and longing of those who take refuge under the wing of your warm visitation. For you see that those in pain take refuge in your sanctuaries as in clinics full of grace where no toil is needed, and they hope for a deliverance from their pains that will not be delayed. For they see you with the mind, even when you are not visible to the eyes. They stretch out their hands. They address you, seeking mercy. They call on you as saviours. They beseech you as guardians. One, who has not yet lost the power to speak, describes in words the pains that grip him and puts forward supplications about them. Another, who because of the extremity of his suffering has lost even his words, sends up groans and reveals the anguish smouldering within. So the one consumed by the blaze of fever holds out his parched tongue in supplication and asks for the dew of your visitation, by the mere sight of you. The one struck by the sharpest pains begs for your sweet help through your visitation. The one who is fainting waits for you as a reviving comfort. The one undone by long wasting looks to your presence to raise him up. The one whose eyes are clouded by disease, who drags out a life of pain, calls you to his help as guides to the light and liberators from pain. Everyone, then, who is clothed in a body subject to many sufferings and bound to its pains asks to receive through you, by the gift of Christ the lover of good, deliverance from the evils that grip him. So nod cheerfully to the supplications of those in need (for this is most characteristic of you, and it is the unfailing hope of those who ask), and fulfil the petitions put before you. Quench the flame of those burning with fever. Lull raging pains. Raise up the limbs of the paralysed. Drive away despondency by restoring good cheer. Call back hopes that have been given up. Rekindle expectations that have died. You are not ignorant of the weakness of nature, not only because you share in it, but also because you have been illumined by God, and through experience itself, [since] those who shared in its evils have been freed through you from their harm, by your heartfelt compassion and visitation.

You know its sluggishness, having experienced it in the misfortunes of others. For you bend with a God-imitating pity toward the fallen. You bear the unpleasantness of foul-smelling sores. With your own hands you labour to raise up those who slip because of it, and you also toil alongside those who try to give it a helping hand. By your very deeds you make them feel that you are present and are setting right what has gone wrong. For the physician, as he sprinkles on saving medicines and asks for the Lord's help, calls on you as helpers in both the asking and the healing. When he seeks to make a fever abate, he asks for your dew-bringing presence. When he takes up the knife and raises his eyes to heaven, he draws down your intercession and lifts it up with his own, and through it he looks for the operation to be safe. When he operates with incisions [?] and tries to remove putrefaction, in desperate cases he looks to you to cut with him and to close the wound with him. Moreover, the one who has come under enemy attack and is worn down by the wars of the godless calls on your intercession to join the battle line. For just as you received invincible power against spiritual enemies and bodily afflictions, so you have received authority from Christ the Almighty against hostile assault, visible battle, and enemy raids. That is why you have pious emperors, together with peoples and cities, joining in supplication to you. So be quick to come before they finish asking, and provide the special people that bears Christ's name with a common healing: the defeat of their enemies. In your goodness, nod to the prayers of those who [?], and ask for them to be unwounded, and for their enemies a rout that brings total destruction. Blunt the edges of the murderous sword. Break the bows of the blasphemers. Burn up the shields of the godless with the fire of your intercession. Silence the voices and words of the boastful. Fetter the tongues that move against the Most High. Make the boast of the pious loud and heard far and wide. Arm those who acknowledge Christ with a greater power. By warm and persistent petitions to the King of all, crown pious emperors with victories and award common trophies to the flock of Christ. You have as your fellow worker the one who supplies abundant gifts; who pours forth rivers of mercy; who opens the abyss of his own graces and helps those who wish to draw from it; whose might is invincible; Christ, who alone gives victory and supplies true peace. You have working with you, in words and in deeds themselves, the Mother of the Giver and Queen of creation. She is the intercessor who is readily heard. In supplication, as in incomparable glory, she is honoured above all immaterial minds and servants of God, and she receives from him, as he grants it, the assurance that her requests will not be refused. Through her human nature, which had fallen sick and lost its true health, was restored to strength, and the spreading of the passions that had grown into it

was checked. Through her the disobedience that brought disease has ceased, and the earthborn race enjoys the healthful virtues of obedience. Through her death-bearing sin was cut off from its flood of evils, and righteousness multiplied in abundance among men. Through her the long tyranny of death has been destroyed. The dead, who had decayed from ages past, were fitted together again by the mighty power of him who was born of her, and were called to ageless life. She became the only untrodden gate of immortal life. Through her the treasuries of incorruption were opened and enriched mortals with immortality. Through her the streams of our forefathers' tears were stopped, and rivers of joy water forever both them and those who understand her great deeds. She is the solemn theme of the angels, their unceasing exultation, and the gladdening boast of human nature. Her grace, at the moment of need, works together with those in distress. It reveals itself as present not to you alone. At such times it also lets those who call on her warmly perceive her own visitation. For they see, as she grants them to see, that at times she directs you to attend to the care of the sick person, and at times she explains the manner of treatment and leaves the whole work of healing to your own hands. She plans and does this not because she declines to come down and stretch out her hand to the sick, or to bring about health by her command alone. For she has the power to nod and bend in love for mankind, beyond what any begotten nature can, yielding to the Son alone the incomparable greatness of compassion. Rather, she does it to honour you as his servants and to confirm the honour given you by your administering this grace. So stir her to intercede, for she is ready, and she pours the oil of compassion lavishly on all. Lull the pains of those who suffer and need healing. Repay the longing of the one who adorns your holy sanctuary and glories in your patronage. And fulfil at all times the petitions of those who have gathered to glorify God and to praise the grace that he has given you. Take as one who offers intercession in harmony with you, both to the Lord who took flesh from her and to her majesty as Mother of God, your own true mother, who imitates her children's love for mankind. You received her as one who nourished you with milk and also brought you to perfection by godly deeds. You had the good fortune to have in her a mother who shared your nature and was of one mind with you in life. Through her you were illumined by the rays of both visible and spiritual light. She is Theodote, who was truly a divine gift, and who brought forth for God acceptable gifts: both her own virtues and you. You have taken her as your partner in good works, and likewise in graces and in boldness before the Creator. Therefore also to

…having taken that very Giver of good things and Cause of all blessings, Christ our God, as the one to whom you make supplication, fulfill the petitions of those who ask. For he himself is the fulfiller and the fullness of the promised benefits. He is their steward and provider, and he both keeps them and offers to share them without stint. To him belong honor and glory and praise and thanksgiving, with the Father and the holy and life-giving Spirit, now and always, and to the ages of ages. Amen.

For the Entry of the Most Holy Theotokos. Let the heaven above rejoice today, and let the clouds rain down gladness at the great and wondrous deeds of our God. For behold, the gate that faces east, born of a barren and fruitless woman according to the promise and consecrated to God as a dwelling, is today brought into the temple as a spotless offering. Let David rejoice as he strikes the lyre: “Virgins shall be brought to the king after her,” he says; “her companions shall be brought.” In the tabernacle of God, within his mercy-seat, [?] to be reared as a dwelling for the one who was born of the Father before the ages without change, for the salvation of our souls. Today the temple that held God, the Theotokos, is brought into the temple of the Lord, and Zechariah receives her. Today the Holy of Holies rejoices, and the choir of angels mystically celebrates. With them let us also, keeping the feast today, cry out with Gabriel: “Hail, full of grace! The Lord is with you, he who has great mercy.” Come, all you peoples, let us praise the only blameless one, foretold by the prophets and offered in the temple, the Mother foreordained before the ages and revealed in the last times as Theotokos. Lord, through her intercessions grant us your peace and great mercy.

For John Chrysostom. Adorned with your golden words as with golden jewelry, O John Chrysostom, the Church rejoices like a bride and cries out to you: “I have drunk my fill of your streams that gush with gold. I am made radiant by gold-gleaming draughts sweet as golden honey. Through your gentle counsels I am led from practice to contemplation, and I am united to Christ, the spiritual Bridegroom, and reign with him.” So we too, gathered on your feast, cry out: Do not tire of interceding with the Lord for us, that our souls may be saved.

For the Holy Fathers of [?] I. The choir of the holy Fathers ran together from the ends of the earth and laid down as dogma the one essence and nature of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, and clearly handed down to the Church the mystery of theology. Let us praise them in faith and call them blessed, saying: O divine army, God-proclaiming soldiers in the Lord's battle line; many-lighted stars of the spiritual firmament; unassailable towers of the mystical Zion; fragrant flowers of paradise; all-golden mouths of the Word; boast of the Church and glory of the world: intercede earnestly for our souls.
